diagrams.title: 01 / Startup and tool discovery
diagrams.subtitle: The local chat backend discovers MCP. Claude does not browse OpenAPI or call localhost.

steps.title: Chat lifespan creates the agent and model adapter
body: Uvicorn serves card_chat.main:app on 8020. Server configuration supplies MODEL_ID and the Anthropic credential. The Cards API is a separate process on 8010 (Docker host port: 8011).

steps.title: Gateway starts a local Python child over stdio
body: connect() launches sys.executable -m card_chat.mcp_server. MCP uses the child's stdin/stdout; diagnostics use stderr. The child does not listen on another HTTP port.

steps.title: Child creates FastMCP and registers create_card
body: FastMCP('Card servicing') constructs the server. @mcp.tool() registers the Python function. mcp.run(transport='stdio') starts the protocol loop. The SDK builds a schema from the function signature.

steps.title: Backend initializes MCP and lists tools
body: ClientSession.initialize() performs the handshake. list_tools() discovers create_card and its inputSchema. Startup checks that it is the only tool.

steps.title: Gateway prepares the model-facing tool schema
body: Copy the discovered schema; remove idempotency_key from properties and required. The workflow retains that key privately. Required card fields remain given_name, user_name and account_number.

steps.title: Only after confirmation does Claude receive a tool
body: During collection: tools are absent from Anthropic requests. After confirmation: the adapter sends the tool name, a configured description and the discovered card-field schema. REST URL/path mapping lives in ApiClient, not in Claude.

diagrams.title: 02 / Each message and the question loop
diagrams.subtitle: Claude extracts intent and values. Python chooses the question and validates completeness.

steps.title: Page starts a conversation, then posts a message
body: POST /conversations returns a conversation ID and greeting. JavaScript stores cid. Send posts {text: ...} to /conversations/{cid}/messages.

steps.title: Retrieve the same Conversation object and append text
body: conversations[cid] contains history, draft, review, submission and a lock. The lock serializes turns. Append the user answer to history; pass history and draft to the agent with allowed_tools={}.

steps.title: Adapter sends instructions plus conversation context
body: AnthropicModel.extract() calls hosted Messages. A system prompt lists supported intents and the three field names, requests JSON, forbids invented values and preserves leading zeros. History and draft are serialized into one user message.

steps.title: Agent interprets extraction and picks a controlled question
body: Extraction validates intent and string-valued fields. The agent merges candidate fields with a copy of the draft. QUESTIONS defines wording and order: given_name, user_name, account_number. It chooses the first missing key. Unsupported actions receive a fixed explanation.

steps.title: Validate updates, then save only actual supplied fields
body: The workflow merges updates with the existing draft. CardCreate enforces trimmed nonblank strings, length limits, no control characters and no extras. Temporary 'pending' values validate partial updates but are never saved or submitted. Invalid updates clear the review and keep the previous draft.

steps.title: Incomplete? Return the next question and repeat
body: Compare saved draft keys with CardCreate.model_fields. If incomplete, save the agent's reply to history and return it. The next request carries the same cid; context is rebuilt from the accumulated history and draft. This state exists only in chat memory.

steps.title: Complete? Fully validate and show a masked review
body: review() validates the complete draft and generates a fresh review token. JavaScript shows Create card when that token is returned. An accepted edit produces a fresh review; the previous token becomes invalid. No card write has happened.

diagrams.title: 03 / Confirmation to REST creation
diagrams.subtitle: A model proposal is checked locally. The workflow executes confirmed values, not model authority.

steps.title: Customer explicitly clicks Create card
body: POST /conversations/{cid}/confirm contains the review token, not a replacement draft. Merely typing 'yes' uses the message route and does not execute MCP.

steps.title: Check review token and freeze the submission
body: Under the conversation lock, reject a stale review with 409. On the first valid click, validate the saved draft, copy it into submission.body, and generate one UUID key. If a successful result is already saved, return it immediately.

steps.title: Agent offers create_card through the Anthropic adapter
body: allowed_tools now contains only create_card with the discovered model-facing schema. propose() sends the confirmed body, forces one named tool call, and disables parallel tool use. Claude returns tool_use with a name and arguments; it does not execute the tool.

steps.title: Approve only a matching proposal
body: Require a ProposedToolCall named create_card. Validate its arguments with CardCreate and compare normalized values with submission.body. Reject mismatches. Call gateway.create with the frozen server-side body and submission key.

steps.title: Gateway dispatches over stdio; MCP calls ApiClient
body: ClientSession.call_tool sends create_card plus body and injected idempotency_key. The registered function validates CardCreate, creates ApiClient using CARD_API_BASE_URL, and invokes its existing create_card method.

steps.title: HTTP POST /cards validates and writes idempotently
body: ApiClient sends JSON and the Idempotency-Key header over HTTP. FastAPI validates CardCreate and the required header, then invokes store.create_idempotent. The normal API uses SQLite. Account existence is assumed; there is no account lookup.

steps.title: Return the actual API result to the browser
body: REST returns 201. MCP validates the Card response and returns {ok, id, card_number}. Chat saves the successful result and formats the final reply. The browser renders textContent. No extra Claude call summarizes the result; errors/timeouts remain retryable with the frozen submission.

diagrams.title: 04 / Idempotency and retries
diagrams.subtitle: Chat prevents duplicate submissions in memory; SQLite durably protects repeated HTTP requests.

steps.title: One confirmation creates one frozen body and key
body: The conversation lock serializes duplicate clicks. The first valid click generates a key; failed attempts keep the same body/key. Completed duplicate clicks return the saved result without calling Claude, MCP or REST again.

steps.title: Normalize and fingerprint the request
body: CardCreate trims surrounding whitespace and validates values. fingerprint() serializes the validated fields with sorted keys and compact JSON, then computes SHA-256. The account remains a string, including its leading zeros.

steps.title: Begin a SQLite write transaction and look up the key
body: BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes writers before checking card_idempotency. Lookup and inserts share one transaction, including across separate API processes using the same SQLite database.

steps.title: Case A: unseen key creates card plus saved response
body: Generate a UUID id and SIM- identifier. Insert cards row and card_idempotency row with key, fingerprint, card_id and original response_json. Commit both together. Return 201 with Idempotency-Replayed: false.

steps.title: Case B: same key and same body replays the card
body: If the stored fingerprint matches, return the saved response instead of inserting. Return 201 with Idempotency-Replayed: true. If a commit succeeded but the first response was lost, retrying the same key/body returns that original card.

steps.title: Case C: same key with a different body is a conflict
body: A fingerprint mismatch raises IdempotencyConflict. The API returns 409; no second card is created. Storage errors return a sanitized 503. The chat retains its submission for an explicit retry rather than generating a fresh key.

steps.title: Boundary: API durability does not restore chat memory
body: SQLite retains cards and committed keys across API restarts. Chat drafts and submission keys disappear on chat restart; do not start a new conversation to retry an uncertain write. A new key means a new operation even when the body is identical.
